clue.text: Whet a sword fashioned for swashbuckling adventure

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens a blade, ready for a bit of pirate-style derring-do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges WHET A SWORD. The title is Charles Kingsley's Victorian novel of Elizabethan sea adventure, also the name of a Devon resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley's novel is a classic tale of seafaring heroics and sword fights against the Spanish.

clue.text: Showed frustration with partners taking part

parts.note: in bridge, West and East play as partners, giving the letters W and E

explanation.surface: Someone got upset when couples insisted on joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'taking' are link words; the bridge pairing of West and East is the convention to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding tears is one way a thwarted person may vent their exasperation.

clue.text: Leg cut as one has to climb quickly

definitions.meaning: a joint of beef taken from the lower foreleg
to scramble up a pole or tree using arms and legs, usually followed by 'up'

explanation.surface: A hurried climber grazes their lower leg on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers sell the lower leg as a cut, and the verb means to clamber up rapidly.

clue.text: Sadistic practice of dropping on one's head

definitions.text: Sadistic practice of dropping on one's head

parts.words: Sadistic practice of dropping on one's head
parts.note: reads like being dropped head-first, but the drops are of liquid falling one by one on a victim's forehead

explanation.surface: A cruel habit of letting someone fall on their skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The torment drips liquid steadily onto a restrained person's forehead until it becomes unbearable.

clue.text: Find new tenant with ease, but forget name

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the word for ease

parts.note: to relent is to ease off or soften

explanation.surface: A landlord fills a flat easily but cannot recall who the occupant is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forget' removes N (name) from RELENT, a synonym for ease (off); 'with' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease out property again to someone else is what a landlord does on finding another occupant.

clue.text: Brill is strong fish

parts.note: hunky means sturdy and muscular
a dory is a flat-bodied sea fish, as in John Dory

explanation.surface: Brill, a flatfish, is described as a powerful fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Brill looks like the flatfish, in keeping with 'fish', but it is British slang short for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for excellent or fine, brill being British slang shortened from brilliant.

clue.text: Poet provided the middle section

indicators.note: asks for the central part of the word provided, dropping two letters from each end

explanation.surface: A poet supplied the central part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, author of the Metamorphoses, is the classic Roman versifier.

clue.text: Novel show of conceit shunned by pilgrim

definitions.meaning: Thackeray's satirical book about Becky Sharp

definitions.text: show of conceit shunned by pilgrim
definitions.meaning: in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, the town fair of worldly pride that Christian refuses to join

explanation.surface: A new display of arrogance is avoided by a religious traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as an adjective for the show, but it is the noun: Thackeray took his title from Bunyan.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's book is titled after the fair in Bunyan's allegory where worldly goods and pride are on sale.

clue.text: Impresario introduces rising girl to detective author

indicators.note: one piece is brought into the middle of the author's name

parts.note: Arthur Conan Doyle wrote the Sherlock Holmes detective stories

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the girl's name is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: Tracy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A theatre producer presents a girl on the up to a crime writer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the girl's name upwards; 'introduces' puts it inside the author's name. Richard D'Oyly Carte staged Gilbert and Sullivan's operas at the Savoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard D'Oyly Carte was the Victorian theatrical producer behind the Savoy operas.

clue.text: Spot vacant, plainly

parts.note: a point is a spot or dot
blank means empty or vacant

explanation.surface: An empty location, described frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking directly and bluntly, without hedging, is speaking in this manner.

clue.text: Black in old slave state.

parts.note: KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky, a slave-holding US state before the Civil War

explanation.surface: Darkness in a former American slaveholding state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink-coloured means very dark, like black ink.

clue.text: Without permission enter passage, making dangerous descent

parts.note: to crash a party is to go in uninvited
a landing is the corridor or space at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A trespasser gets into a corridor and has a perilous fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft forced down in an emergency comes down hazardously, often damaging itself.

clue.text: Quite attractive, or excessively so?

parts.note: pretty means quite or fairly, as in pretty good
pretty means good-looking

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is fairly good-looking or overdone in its charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' points back to 'attractive': the doubled word means prettified to excess, cutesy.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated form means overdone in its charm, cloyingly decorative.

clue.text: In Carol, Scrooge's clerk losing appeal and having to withdraw

indicators.note: the shortened clerk's name goes inside the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing

indicators.note: the clerk's name drops a part, the word for appeal

parts.note: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
IT means sex appeal

explanation.surface: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol, Bob Cratchit loses his charm and must pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Carol points to Dickens's book, but it is a verb. Scratching a horse means withdrawing it from a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor pulled out of a race before the start is described as being scratched.

clue.text: Complain over space set up as area for sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first word sits above the second

parts.note: to grouse is to grumble

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for space is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a room being arranged as a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ROOM into MOOR. A grouse moor is upland heather where game birds are shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathland managed for shooting game birds is a field where a sporting pursuit takes place.

clue.text: Abrasive ruler in vehicle on a celebratory occasion

indicators.note: the ruler's letter goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A harsh monarch rides in a car to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' supplies its own letters rather than linking. A carbonado is a black diamond used in drills and as an abrasive.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark, impure diamond is used industrially for grinding and cutting, so it serves as a scouring material.

clue.text: Chemical works are inland

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order, as works suggests reshaping

explanation.surface: A chemical plant is situated away from the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' reads as a noun (a factory) but is the anagram signal for ARE INLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: This hormone released by the adrenal glands is a biochemical substance.

clue.text: Capital seat one's sunk into

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat
one is the Roman numeral I; 's means is

explanation.surface: Someone flops down into a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Unlike the boys in blue?

definitions.meaning: blue means pornographic, as in an X-rated film

explanation.surface: Asking how someone differs from the policemen in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boys in blue' suggests police, but the clue splits into two senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is no longer a boy, and an X-rated film is also called blue.

clue.text: Normality disrupted in money-making enterprise

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Business as usual breaks down at a profitable firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges NORMALITY. 'money-making' is literal: the Royal Mint is the UK body that makes coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The national coin manufacturer literally produces currency.

clue.text: One should maintain one's balance, jumping over mound

parts.note: a hurdler clearing a fence jumps over it
a bank is a raised mound of earth

explanation.surface: A rider must keep steady while leaping a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a tip about physical steadiness, but balance is money held in an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a bank holds customers' current accounts and settles cheques between banks, keeping their funds.

clue.text: Sailor capsized with second person in marshy inlet

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the sailor's letters are turned over

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
you is the second-person pronoun in grammar

explanation.surface: A sailor overturned in a swampy creek along with another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns AB into BA; 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In the southern US, a slow-moving swampy creek or outlet of a river is called this.

clue.text: Nothing to write about poor labourer

indicators.note: the word for write goes around the zero

parts.note: to pen is to write
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing to record concerning an impoverished worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PEN round O.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin America, a landless farmhand or day worker is called this.

clue.text: Member's thrown out by jerk in this joint

definitions.text: Member's thrown out by jerk in this joint

parts.words: Member's thrown out by jerk in this joint
parts.note: member is a limb: when a doctor taps below this leg joint, the lower leg kicks out in the reflex jerk

explanation.surface: A club member is expelled by an idiot from this seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Member, jerk and joint all suggest a club ejecting a fool from a dive; they are a limb, a reflex and a body hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor's reflex test taps just below this leg joint, making the lower leg kick out.

clue.text: Implacable element in press

definitions.meaning: unbending, as in a will of steel
to smooth clothes flat with a hot appliance

explanation.surface: A relentless factor in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal Fe gives a word for unyielding firmness and for pressing creases out of laundry.

clue.text: Animal on the ground a long time — shoot it

indicators.note: in an across clue, the animal comes after the ground

parts.note: clay is soil or earth
a pig is an animal
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A beast lies on the earth for ages, and someone says to fire at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hunting a live animal, but the 'animal' is the target hurled into the air for shooting practice.
explanation.definitionFit: The disc flung from a trap is what a sporting marksman fires at.

clue.text: Foreigner without an original idea

indicators.note: the word for foreigner loses the letters of an

parts.note: a German is a foreigner to a British setter

explanation.surface: An outsider lacks creative thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes AN from GERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed or kernel of a notion, from which more develops, is called this.

clue.text: Spoiling clue with ending that's absurd

indicators.note: absurd suggests nonsense, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword clue is ruined by a ridiculous finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' rearranges CLUE and ENDING together; 'with' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampering or giving in to every wish is lavish treatment of a child or oneself.
